title: Signal and Orbit
premise: Marguerite Sandoval has spent eleven years alone on Relay Station Kestrel, translating the beacon's impossible signal and slowly forgetting how to dream in any human tongue. When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the whole system, she discovers the beacon is a forgery she unknowingly maintains: a fake armistice signal keeping two hostile fleets in stalemate. As the real architects close in to silence her, Marguerite must choose between exposing the lie that could ignite war and protecting the ragtag crew of salvagers who have become her first family. In the end, she broadcasts a new signal of her own design — a language built from her dreams — forcing both fleets to confront the truth together, and choosing found family over the duty that consumed her.
about_author: Ada Pemberton is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about the people history forgets to record. She lives near a decommissioned listening station, where she claims the static still talks to her.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A day in her isolated routine: calibrating the beacon, logging signals, talking to the station AI, Ossuary, as if it were company. She dreams in colors and geometry now, not words. Emotional beat: loneliness so deep it has become identity.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Gravity flickers system-wide; coffee rises, dust orbits, and every screen fills with cascading errors. The beacon transmits something unauthorized during those nine seconds. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as she realizes she is not alone in this event.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Dez Okonkwo's POV, captain of the salvage tug Long Odds. His crew limps toward Kestrel seeking shelter after the flicker crippled their drive. They find a station everyone believed decommissioned. Emotional beat: wary curiosity; Dez recognizes a fellow ghost when he sees one.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Says
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marguerite decrypts the nine-second burst with Dez's engineer, Priya: the beacon carries a forged cease-fire protocol, decades old, signed by no living authority. Emotional beat: vertigo — her life's work is a load-bearing lie.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Through black-market channels the crew learns both the Concord fleet and the Meridian flotilla obey the beacon as gospel. Whoever controls Kestrel controls the peace. A Concord patrol pings the station. Emotional beat: the dawning weight of consequence.

chapters.title: The Architects
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A covert Concord vessel arrives carrying Vess Andrade, one of the beacon's original designers, who orders Marguerite to keep transmitting and say nothing. Vess reveals the flicker means the forgery is failing. Emotional beat: betrayal — Marguerite was never hired; she was hidden.

chapters.title: Dream Grammar
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Unable to sleep, she maps her non-human dreams against the beacon's structure and realizes they share a grammar — the signal was partly derived from something genuinely alien, something the architects buried. Emotional beat: reclamation of self through language.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Meridian scouts board the Long Odds; the crew hides Vess and the decryption data while Marguerite stalls via translation, buying hours with improvised diplomacy. Ossuary begins dying under attack. Emotional beat: terror transformed into fierce protectiveness of her chosen family.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, climax. With both fleets converging on Kestrel, Marguerite rejects Vess's demand to renew the old lie. Instead she transmits her dream-language — truth about the forgery braided with the alien grammar — forcing both fleets to receive the same confession simultaneously. Emotional beat: sacrifice of safety for honesty.

chapters.title: Signal and Orbit
chapters.summary: Dez's POV, resolution. The fleets hold fire, shaken into negotiation by shared revelation; Vess surrenders her archives. The Long Odds stays docked at Kestrel, its crew refusing to leave. Marguerite dreams, for the first time in years, in two languages at once. Emotional beat: belonging — duty replaced by family.
